Hi Anya / Marco —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call plus proposed next steps so we’re aligned heading into the technical deep dive: 

Key pain points you reiterated:
- High tail latency during peak trading hours (95th pctl spikes to ~350ms), which causes front-end timeouts and degraded UX.
- Cost unpredictability when nightly batch inference runs overlap with interactive traffic.
- Concern about prompt latency amplification when using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) across large corpora.

Goals you asked us to prioritize:
1) Bring 95th pctl interactive latency down to <=120ms for the core LLM-driven features (conservative SLA target).
2) Have a predictable cost envelope for steady-state QPS with burst capacity for nightly jobs.
3) Maintain model quality within 2% of current outputs for top-1 intents (we discussed a light eval suite).

Technical constraints / model details you shared:
- Working with a finetuned family based on Llama2-13B (8-bit quantized in prod), and a 70B variant used for high-quality summaries in nightly jobs.
- Average request size is ~600 tokens (prompt+expected completion), typical interactive sequence length 128 tokens.
- KV cache blowup: some requests reuse long prefixes (session-based chat).

Proposed deployment pathways (high-level):
A) Dedicated (reserved GPUs) for interactive traffic: pin a quantized 13B variant, use small-batch continuous batching + prefix KV caching to hit 95th pctl target.
B) Hosted burst / private for nightly 70B jobs: route to prewarmed capacity with autoscale window and temporary quota bump to avoid interfering with interactive SLOs.
C) Canary / multi-variant routing: route 10% of traffic to 13B vs fallback 70B for quality-sensitive paths with automatic rollback.

Immediate next steps (action owners):
- Bridgehead: share a sample traffic trace (CSV with timestamp, latency, token counts) and the RAG vector-store size estimate (Marco) — due 2026-10-09.
- Redwood: produce a short topology sketch (attached) and KV-cache sizing spreadsheet; include estimated instance counts and expected QPS per instance (Soojin, Rishi) — due 2026-10-09.
- Technical deep dive to align on exact SLOs and canary plan: Schedule a 60-minute session next week with engineering (Rishi to lead).

Attachments: redwood-deploy-sketch.pdf (high-level topology), kv-cache-sizing.csv (initial sizing template).

Notes on quantization and latency levers (brief):
- For interactive traffic the plan is to use 8-bit quantized kernels with attention optimizations; this reduces memory and enables larger batch windows while keeping latency bounded.
- Prefix/KV caching is the highest ROI for your workload because of repeated session prefixes; we’ll model cache hit-rate impact on effective token compute.
- If you need strict <50ms p95 we’ll discuss sharding the model across multiple GPUs and local inference nodes near edge regions, but that has cost implications.

Proposed times for the technical deep dive: 2026-10-12 or 2026-10-13 between 09:00–12:00 PT. Let me know which works for you.

Thanks — looking forward to the traces so Rishi can run a quick capacity estimate.

Best,

Soojin / team — ran a preliminary estimate against the traffic numbers Anya shared in the trace (thanks). Summary: 

- Baseline assumptions: 13B quantized at 8-bit, avg interactive sequence 128 tokens, avg infer time per token ~0.9ms on the target GPU (Ampere-class with optimized kernels). 
- Effective per-request compute: ~115ms (compute-only) for a 128-token completion; add ~10–20ms for I/O + scheduling in the runtime.
- With continuous adaptive batching and a 75% cache hit rate (their session reuse pattern), effective p95 latency reduces by ~40% vs cold runs.

Sizing (p95-provisioned, conservative 80% utilization):
- Steady median QPS 85 -> need ~5 inference instances (each sustaining ~18 QPS at p95 with batching).
- Peak overlap QPS 320 -> burst capacity of ~18 instances (autoscale pool / reserved) to prevent p95 degradation.

Recommendation / ops notes:
- Use dedicated reserved pool for interactive (5 primary instances, autoscale to 20 for headroom).
- Nightly 70B jobs: schedule during a clearly defined window and put a capacity guard (priority routing) so they never evict interactive instances. Consider running those in the private deployment or separate region.
- KV cache sizing: with 24-hr retention their estimated cache memory is ~420GB across nodes; trimming to 4 hours reduces to ~160GB. This affects instance memory footprints for 13B.

I attached the quick CSV with per-instance QPS assumptions and a rough cost delta for reserved vs burst. Happy to iterate on the deep dive.

—Rishi
